name: NY-10
label: Safe D

key_factors: Open seat after Goldman lost renomination, but Lander is a well-funded, high-profile nominee
Republican nominee has no reported fundraising
model.rationale: The D+32 baseline and fundamentals point to a Safe Democratic hold, and prediction markets agree at 98%. Lander's strong primary win and the GOP nominee's lack of visible resources justify keeping the margin near the baseline.
model.watch: Any late polling showing an unusually weak Democratic nominee or a surge of outside spending against Lander could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Dan Goldman (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Dan Goldman lost renomination, leaving this deep-blue Brooklyn-based seat open, but the district's D+32 partisan lean makes it overwhelmingly Democratic territory. Brad Lander, the New York City comptroller, won the Democratic nomination and enters the general election as the heavy favorite. His Republican opponent, Jennifer Moore, has no reported fundraising or cash on hand, giving her little means to compete.

The quantitative baseline puts the expected Democratic margin at roughly 29 points, and prediction markets price a Democratic win at about 98 percent. With no general-election polls or expert ratings available, the forecast rests on fundamentals, which all point the same direction. This is a Safe Democratic seat.
